1.title: CVE-2026-112354 (CVSS 9.8)
1.summary: Etrel INCH AC charging station management web interface prior to firmware versions 7.1.2 and 8.0.1 contains a hard-coded default credentials vulnerability that allows remote attackers to gain full Administrator access by authenticating with the factory-default account. Attackers can log in over cleartext HTTP to obtain complete charger configuration, OCPP ChargePoint Identity, and CSMS WebSocket connection details, enabling unauthorized administrative control of the charging station.

1.title: CVE-2026-121597 (CVSS 9.9)
1.summary: A weakness has been identified in TOTOLINK A950RG 4.1.2cu.5268_B20221104. This affects the function setAppEasyWizardConfig of the file /cgi-bin/cstecgi.cgi of the component Easy Setup Wizard Handler. Executing a manipulation of the argument functionType can lead to stack-based buffer overflow. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks.

1.title: CVE-2026-121598 (CVSS 9.9)

1.title: CVE-2026-121600 (CVSS 9.9)

1.title: CVE-2026-121606 (CVSS 10.0)
1.summary: A vulnerability has been found in Qihoo 360 D621-2, D603-2, D600-2, D619, D606-6 and D706 up to 6.4.9. Affected by this issue is the function verify_sign of the file fs2/bin/iscm of the component Firmware Signature Verification. 1.title: The Classics Return: Vulnerable E-Mail Scripts, (Wed, Nov 4th)
1.summary: One of the early web application vulnerabilities I remember was CVE-2000-0411 [CVE]. This was a simple vulnerability in a CGI-bin script used to send e-mail. The vulnerability was pretty straightforward: Adding additional parameters to the URL leaked environment variables. Other vulnerabilities allowed setting the "To" address and were heavily abused by spammers. And if parameters were passed directly to the sendmail binary, similar vulnerabilities could allow arbitrary code execution.

1.title: CVE-2026-119977 — WordPress WordPress Core Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition Vulnerability
1.summary: Vendor/product: WordPress WordPress Core. WordPress WordPress Core contains a time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on the server during the upgrade window. This is due to predictable, web-accessible staging paths used during full-package core upgrades. Required action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines. Due date: 2026-11-06. Known ransomware use: Unknown.

1.title: GHSA-gh9r-c94j-cmp5 — Stanza: RCE via pickle deserialization in the lemmatizer
1.summary:
## TL;DR

Loading an attacker-supplied lemma `.pt` runs arbitrary code as the loading user. Since 1.14.0 the lemmatizer stores `pos_dict` as a gzip-compressed pickle in the checkpoint's `dicts` field (a `bytes` value). `torch.load(weights_only=True)` treats `bytes` as a primitive and passes it through unexamined, so its allowlist never sees the inner stream. `Trainer.load` then feeds those bytes to an **unrestricted `pickle.loads`**: the only bare `pickle.loads` in the tree. Result: `weights_only=True` gives no protection here, and model loading executes code.

1.title: GHSA-7w38-ggh5-v542 — Elo Ruby backend has Remote Code Execution via unescaped `#{...}` interpolation in emitted string literals and subtype-constraint labels
1.summary:
### Summary

Elo's Ruby backend emits attacker-controlled text into Ruby double-quoted strings without escaping the `#` character. Because `#` begins Ruby's interpolation sequences — `#{expr}`, `#@ivar`, `#@@cvar`, `#$gvar` — and any expression wrapped in `#{...}` may use backticks for shell execution, an Elo program that contains a crafted string literal or a labelled subtype constraint compiles to Ruby that evaluates attacker-chosen Ruby, and through backticks runs attacker-chosen shell commands, at runtime.

1.title: GHSA-x9rp-7wh3-2rj5 — Elo backends have code injection via unvalidated emission of programmatic AST fields
1.summary:
### Summary

Elo's programmatic AST API accepts arbitrary values in many node fields without runtime type or syntax validation. Each backend's emit stage interpolates those values straight into the generated source with no escape pass. An integrator that populates the AST from JSON-deserialised input, plugin output, or any other untyped source therefore exposes a code-injection primitive that flows through to the emitted JavaScript, Ruby, Python, or SQL.

1.title: GHSA-j97h-3f8r-mrjr — Keycloak has authentication bypass via jwt algorithm confusion
1.summary:
### Description
A flaw was found in Keycloak. This JWT algorithm confusion vulnerability in the JWT Authorization Grant flow allows an attacker with valid client credentials to bypass signature verification. By forging an assertion, the attacker can create unauthorized access tokens. This enables the attacker to impersonate any federated user linked to the affected Identity Provider, leading to unauthorized access and potential privilege escalation.

1.title: GHSA-h26j-4vp7-x9w2 — Metalama: Unsafe deserialization over Metalama's Visual Studio inter-process named pipe enables local code execution
1.summary:
## Summary

Metalama uses a local named-pipe channel to communicate between its Visual Studio processes — the Visual Studio UI process (`devenv`), the out-of-process Roslyn code-analysis process, and the CodeLens process. This channel deserialized messages from the pipe **without restricting which CLR types could be instantiated**. A local process able to write to the pipe can send a crafted message that instantiates arbitrary .NET types — a deserialization primitive in the same class as `BinaryFormatter` (CWE-502), and a well-known gadget-chain code-execution vector.
